release_contents: PRIORITY 1.1, admin-erp side: App\Services\PublicSiteRevalidator + HomepageCarouselSlideObserver. After ANY change to a homepage-carousel slide (create, edit, image replace, reorder, toggle, delete — one observer covers all of them) Laravel sends a signed POST to {PUBLIC_SITE_URL}/api/revalidate so the Next.js site drops its cached carousel immediately instead of after its 120s fetch window. HMAC-SHA256 over '<unix-timestamp>.<tag>'; the secret is never transmitted. Queued and sent from a terminating callback (after the response), 5s/3s timeouts, every failure caught and logged, de-duplicated per request (a reorder saves two rows but sends one call), and skipped entirely when no secret is configured. 8 new tests; full suite green in the build gate (mariadb_test_suite true). No migration.
switch_note: Clean switch at 2026-10-02T11:58:02Z: atomic_rename_ms 0.241, public_asset_sync_ms 8.4, routes_changed false, all cache rebuilds exit 0 (config:cache is what picked up REVALIDATE_SECRET from the live .env), and the public_uploads_persisted gate passed (sentinel sha256 identical across the swap) for the THIRD consecutive release.

post_deploy_production_e2e: PRIORITY 1.1 measured against the live site, driving the real Admin endpoints and polling the real homepage: create 287ms and 316ms, disable 458ms, re-enable 254ms, reorder 285ms (new order verified), replace image 741ms, delete 926ms and 578ms, all visible on the FIRST poll after the admin response. Before this release the same changes took up to 120s. Re-verified with a second round of QA slides after the final institutional build: create 897ms and 1536ms. All QA slides and their files were removed; verified via the public API, the live homepage, and the file API (only the owner's own slide and image remain). No orphan files.

cron_timing_note: Cron runs in UTC. One-shot crons scheduled 5-8 minutes ahead on specific minutes, read once via the cron-jobs output operation, then deleted immediately — none left armed (verified empty via a cron-jobs list call after smoke-test-live). One migrate-apply create-cron call in this deploy failed client-side with a transient DNS error (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND developers.hostinger.com) before reaching Hostinger at all; a cron-jobs list call confirmed no job had actually been created, so the retry was safe and did not double-schedule anything — worth that same list-to-confirm check any time a cron-create call itself errors, rather than assuming it's safe (or unsafe) to retry blind.
release_manager_path_reminder: release-manager.php lives at the PRIVATE path /home/u951246149/domains/provatferi.org/laravel-admin-releases/_tooling/release-manager.php for every step after the one-time install — NOT under public_html/admin/. The upload step's own generateUploadURLV1 call must target the domain admin.provatferi.org (the subdomain itself), not the parent provatferi.org — the parent domain's upload URL roots at that domain's own public_html (wrong tree entirely for this subdomain's docroot), while the subdomain's own upload URL roots directly at its docroot, matching upload-release.mjs's un-prefixed `_release_staging/...` destination path exactly.
never_fetch_a_staged_script_url: Requesting a staged one-shot script's URL EXECUTES it (it is under the web-servable docroot). Verify removal with the file listing tool instead.

curl_csrf_testing_note: When scripting a POST to a CSRF-protected route (e.g. /locale) with curl, fetch the CSRF token and set the cookie jar in the SAME request that will be reused for the POST, not across separate GET calls with the jar re-opened each time — doing it in two disjoint GET calls produced a spurious 419 in an earlier session even though the actual endpoint was working correctly.
monorepo_note: admin-erp/ and institutional/ are two subdirectories of ONE git repository (same origin remote, same commit history) — a commit that only touches one of the two still shares a SHA history with the other. build-release.sh already handles this correctly (it has throughout this engagement): it archives and ships only the admin-erp/ subtree for this pipeline. The institutional/ subtree of the exact same commit ships separately through that site's own deploy mechanism (git archive + Hostinger Node build + CDN purge) — the two deploys are independent operations against the same commit, not one combined step.
public_uploads_fix: RESOLVED 2026-10-02. Storage::disk(public) had been returning 404 URLs since the first release because the stock root (storage/app/public) needs storage:link and symlink() is disabled on this host. Root moved to public_html/admin/storage (the vhost docroot) - web-served directly, never renamed by the atomic switch, never pruned by the additive public-asset sync, so uploads persist across releases with no sync step. public_path() was rejected because it lives inside laravel-admin/ and would be renamed away to _previous-* on every switch. See deploy/remote/lib/public-uploads.php and tests/Feature/Deploy/PublicUploadsContractTest.php.
production_e2e_priority0: Full owner-specified E2E passed. Real image uploaded through the live Admin UI landed in public_html/admin/storage/homepage-carousel/ and was immediately HTTP 200 (image/png, exact byte count). Real Chrome (scripts/screenshot.mjs) then reported ok:true on provatferi.org - zero failed requests, zero broken images, zero console errors - where the same page before the fix reported ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB on the carousel image. A second full deploy was then run: the image uploaded BEFORE it still served HTTP 200 afterwards with an sha256 identical to the locally-generated original. Delete through Admin removed the file from disk (verified via the file API; a lingering HTTP 200 immediately after a delete is Hostinger CDN edge cache, not a failed delete). The owner's own pre-existing slide image was migrated forward automatically by stage() and now renders.
cron_chaining_note: Cron commands on this host cannot chain: && is mangled by the API's escaping (the command silently does not run) and ; only returns the LAST command's output. One action per cron. This is why release-manager.php gained a  action that chains the pre-switch stages inside PHP instead.

It is NOT in git, NOT in any build artifact (the institutional archive was grep-verified to contain zero occurrences), and NOT NEXT_PUBLIC_.
